speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The Gas Act was last amended in 2007 to enhance market access and strengthen safeguards for critical infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: To meet this demand in a secure and competitive manner, we have built a liquefied natural gas (LNG) terminal to supplement our piped natural gas (PNG) supply.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The LNG terminal has also enabled new business opportunities in a variety of ancillary services, such as trading, bunkering and break-bulking, which have enhanced the dynamism of our gas market.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Against the backdrop of these developments in our energy markets, it is necessary to update the Gas Act to ensure that it remains effective and relevant.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: In finalising these amendments, MTI and EMA sought feedback from industry stakeholders and members of the public through a public consultation in June earlier this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: MTI and EMA have carefully considered all feedback received and incorporated them where relevant.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Singapore relies heavily on imported natural gas as fuel for power generation and as industrial feedstock, and any gas supply emergency can adversely affect our economy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: These directions may include empowering EMA to reallocate gas from users who can use alternative fuels to those who have no alternative fuel supplies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: These directions may also include requiring relevant parties to enter into, modify or terminate contractual agreements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Persons who comply with the direction will be protected from legal liability, if doing so results in breach of an existing contractual obligation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The Bill further defines that a "severe gas shortage situation" occurs when there is a shortage of natural gas imported into Singapore that results in gas importers being unable to fulfil their contractual obligations to end-users and where the extent, and likely duration or uncertainty of the period, of the gas shortage is likely to threaten the security or stability of gas or electricity supply in Singapore or result in a severe loss of industrial or economic output.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The amendment is worded as such to provide EMA with the flexibility to react to the wide range of potential threats that may emerge.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: In addition, parties can seek compensation for losses or damage suffered as a result of complying with EMA's directions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The compensation will be determined by an independent panel set up under the Gas Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The second amendment, in clause 3 of the Bill, amends section 3 of the Gas Act to enhance EMA's regulation of gas-related activities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Presently, EMA's regulatory functions under the Gas Act include "protecting the public from dangers arising from the production, processing, storage, conveyance, shipping, supply or use of gas".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: To cover the broader value chain of gas-related activities, clause 3 of the Bill expands these regulatory functions to include protecting the public from dangers to health arising from such gas-related activities, including the import of gas, which is presently not included.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This strengthens regulation over a broader spectrum of gas-related activities and expands EMA's regulatory control over technical requirements for gas imports to include thresholds for harmful substances, such as sulphur compounds and heavy metals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The third amendment, in clause 8 of the Bill, expands the scope of "designated gas licensees" under Part VIIB of the Gas Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: These are licensees who require EMA's approval for changes in ownership, and board and chief executive officer appointments, in view of their strategic importance to our gas system.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: To allow flexibility to designate gas licensees as the gas industry evolves, the amendment will also empower the Minister to specify other gas licensees as "designated gas licensees", going forward if the need arises.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The fourth amendment, in clause 22 of the Bill, amends sections 33 and 34 of the Gas Act to expand the scope of the Special Administration Order (SAO), to provide EMA with greater flexibility to deal with unforeseen emergency scenarios.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Presently, an SAO can only be issued in relation to the gas transporter and LNG terminal operator licensees.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The amendment will expand the scope of the SAO to cover any gas licensee.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This will bring the SAO provisions in the Gas Act in line with those in the Electricity Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: MTI and EMA have also incorporated feedback from the industry to make it clear that the SAO can be issued in relation to some, and not necessarily all, of the affairs, business and property of licensees.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This will enable the SAO to be tailored to the gas-related business of licensees whose business include non-gas related parts, as may be appropriate in the circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The Gas Act currently prohibits a gas licensee from applying for a JM.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The intent is to ensure that critical licensees are not unilaterally placed under JM and dissolved.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: However, this restricts non-critical licensees from applying for a JM even though their restructuring or exit would not adversely impact our energy security and system stability.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Hence, the amendment allows JM of a licensee if EMA's consent is obtained.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Submarine gas pipelines within Singapore's territorial waters convey imported natural gas to our gas network.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Damage to these pipelines can disrupt Singapore's gas and electricity supply and result in high economic losses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Presently, damage to any submarine gas pipeline is an offence under the Merchant Shipping Act that carries a maximum fine of only $50,000 and/or imprisonment of up to two years upon conviction.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This is too low to effectively deter damage to submarine gas pipelines.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This is a calibrated increase compared to the $1 million fine and/or imprisonment of up to five years for damage to land-based gas pipelines.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The seventh amendment, in clause 5 of the Bill, amends section 32A of the Gas Act to rationalise the different offences currently provided in the section, which include offences relating to damage to land-based gas transmission infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Such infrastructure is critical in ensuring the flow of gas to businesses and households.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The amendment also seeks to extend the reach of the section by making a person who causes or permits another person to damage land-based gas transmission infrastructure guilty of an offence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: There is no need for the former to have any particular relationship with the latter.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The penalty for offences under this section remains unchanged as a maximum fine of $1 million and/or imprisonment of up to five years upon conviction.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Beyond enhancing protection of critical gas infrastructure, there is a need to effectively deter the dishonest consumption of gas and tampering of gas meters.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The dishonest consumption of gas presently carries a maximum fine of $50,000 and/or imprisonment for a term of up to five years upon conviction.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This amendment takes into consideration that the cost of the gas that is dishonestly consumed is borne by all paying consumers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This enhances deterrence by ensuring proportionality between the penalty imposed and the value of gas dishonestly consumed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The ninth amendment, also in clause 7 of the Bill, expands section 47 of the Gas Act to specify that it is an offence to do anything that compromises or affects the ability of a meter in registering the quantity of gas supplied to any person or premises.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This amendment will enable EMA to prosecute persons who use novel or unconventional methods to tamper with meters, with a view to dishonestly consume gas.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Part IX of the Gas Act presently empowers EMA to regulate anti-competitive practices and conduct in the Singapore gas market.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: To facilitate competition in the gas market, the 10th amendment, in clause 15 of the Bill, introduces a new section 72A to the Gas Act that enables EMA to issue guidelines to inform the gas market regarding practices and conduct that are anti-competitive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This amendment is consistent with the Competition Act, which similarly allows the Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore (CCCS) to publish guidelines to guide market behaviour.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: To ensure that the industry’s views are incorporated, EMA will consult the industry when formulating these guidelines.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: First, clause 20 of the Bill amends section 93 of the Gas Act to enable regulations to be made to specify the procedures for submission of appeals to and consideration of appeals by the Minister regarding EMA’s regulatory decisions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This will enable regulations requiring the facts, issues and grounds of appeal to be set out clearly when appeals are made and enable the Minister to reject appeals that do not meet these requirements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Confidential and sensitive information submitted in appeals will also be safeguarded.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This will facilitate consideration of appeals by the Minister and bring the Gas Act in line with existing appeal provisions in other Acts, such as the Telecommunications Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Last, clause 19 of the Bill inserts a new section 92A to provide for various moneys collected by EMA under the Gas Act to be paid into the Consolidated Fund.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Hon Speaker Mr Tan Chuan-Jin and hon Members of Parliament, I support this Bill as it strengthens and tightens the Gas Act to safeguard our future.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Today, I wish to speak on three areas, mainly, energy security, energy sustainability and energy resilience.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: On energy security, almost every Singaporean knows that we are a vulnerable and small nation with almost zero natural resources.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: But not as many may realise the extent to which we rely on imported fuel to meet our energy demands.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: For our security, I feel it is important that we should not be beholden to any country to meet our energy needs.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: So, we have to take this Bill very seriously for now and our future generations as, without the natural gas, our power generation will be disrupted and Singapore will be in total darkness.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: And with the opening of the Singapore natural gas terminal in 2014, I am glad to see Singapore diversifying our sources of supply to include LNG.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: In this regard, could the Senior Parliamentary Secretary share with us if these contracts will be renewed or will we make the switch to LNG upon expiry of these contracts?

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Also, with the expected increase in worldwide demand for LNG, how are we looking to stabilise the market price fluctuations and deliver a reliable and stable service and, more importantly, keep an affordable price point for Singaporeans?

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: On a related point, I commend the Singapore LNG Corporation on expanding its capacity over the years.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: I understand that there will be a second terminal that will strengthen Singapore’s position.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore is in a unique situation, located in the Straits of Malacca, with important shipping access that serves all major shipping lines.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore’s strategic geographical location allows for easier access to the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and Southeast Asian countries.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Globally, Singapore is also well-known as the financial and commodity trading hub of Asia.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: On energy sustainability, in my work with Singaporean youths, I have met many who feel strongly in preserving the environment.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: As part of this, many support switching from fossil fuel to renewable energy.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Towards this, I commend good initiatives, such as the JTC's SolarRoof project, Treelodge@Punggol, deployment of Solar Photovoltaics (PVs) in reservoirs across Singapore and building Singapore’s first micro-grid living lab in Pulau Ubin.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: I believe we should make a stronger push about going into solar energy.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: For example, in Japan, Toyota has come up with a green coating to coat buildings to keep them cool by as much as 30%.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Such green innovation ensures the efficiency of cooling down our buildings which will translate into great cost savings in electricity bills for the consumers.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Our founding Prime Minister Mr Lee Kuan Yew reminded us repeatedly that we have to take the world as it is, and not as we wish it to be.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: We are not immune to cybersecurity attacks or major energy disruptions.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: The incident emphasised the need for Singapore to be energy-resilient.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Although the disruption was due to a partial loss of electricity supply from two power generation companies, we cannot take it lightly.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: In that light, it is important that all Singaporeans are equipped with the skills and knowledge to remain calm and resilient in any such emergencies.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Perhaps carrying out an awareness campaign or public education drive is something that can be considered.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: It is a strength to know what to do if the lights are out.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: At the core of that resilient spirit, Singaporeans must not take our energy supply for granted and must give credit where it is due and to commend the Government, MTI and EMA for ensuring the energy supplies of Singapore and for taking all possible steps to mitigate any shortage or disruptions over the years.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: As a small country without any natural resources, Singapore imports nearly all of our energy needs.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Prior to 2013, we were completely reliant on Malaysia and Indonesia for our natural gas supply, which is transported to us via pipes.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: As the Member has noted, our piped gas contracts are set to expire over the next decade or so.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: As all of our gas supply is handled commercially, whether our piped gas contracts are renewed will depend on commercial negotiations.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: And we welcome renewals or new contracts for piped gas.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: In October 2017, EMA lifted its moratorium on new piped gas contracts to facilitate this.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: To enhance our energy security and competitiveness, the Government has pursued diversification of our gas sources as a strategy.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We have also adopted a Competitive Licensing Framework to procure LNG on a tranche-by-tranche basis.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: This will provide Singapore with the flexibility to take advantage of opportunities in the global gas market, including more competitive price indexation and contract terms, while diversifying our gas sources to reinforce our supply security.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: To further strengthen our energy security, we have also added capacity to the LNG terminal ahead of demand, providing us with spare capacity to cater for any potential disruption in our piped natural gas supply.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: The Government will continue to plan ahead for our next phase of LNG infrastructure development.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We are currently exploring several options to see which best meet our long-term LNG needs and further improve our energy security.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: As I have highlighted earlier, the proposed amendment in clause 14 of the Bill will further enhance EMA's ability to deal with a wide range of potential risks that may emerge.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: It empowers EMA to issue directions to require any person to take measures to address or alleviate the severe gas shortage or prevent it from occurring or continuing.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Beyond meeting our domestic energy requirements, we have been taking steps to capitalise on our strategic location to develop Singapore as a regional gas hub.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Our LNG terminal can conduct storage and reloads, and we have spare capacity available for trading.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We have also been working with the industry to build a strong supporting ecosystem, with players, such as consulting firms, law firms, shipbrokers, price reporting agencies and other services providers.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: All these and more have established their presence in Singapore, adding to the depth of the ecosystem.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: And to further increase dynamism in our gas market, EMA has also formalised the spot LNG import framework in October 2017.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: So, interested parties can now import spot LNG, subject to a market-wide cap of 10% of our long-term contracted gas sales agreements.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: In summary, there is actually a whole-of-ecosystem approach to looking at our energy resilience.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Singapore is exploring other ways to broaden our energy options.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Among the renewable energy options, solar PV has the greatest potential for wider deployment in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: But even then, there are challenges to adopting solar energy at scale, for example, competing uses for limited land, and the intermittency of the electricity generated by solar PV due to high cloud cover and urban shading.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Despite these challenges, we have grown the amount of solar PV deployed from 10 megawatt peak (MWp) in 2012 to more than 160 MWp today.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We are planning to raise our solar generation capacity to 350 MWp by 2020 and to one GWp beyond 2020.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We are also investing in research and development to increase the efficiency of solar PV and the accuracy of forecasting solar power output in our tropical climate.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: This includes testbeds on utility-scale energy storage systems that could facilitate greater deployment of solar PV in Singapore while ensuring that our power system's security, reliability and stability are not compromised.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: My colleague, Senior Minister of State Koh Poh Koon, had spoken about this during question time, but if I may just share again.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: In the design of any electricity grid system, we have to balance redundancy and assurance with cost imposed on consumers.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: The higher the degree of redundancy, the smaller the probability of disruption, the higher the cost at the system level.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: So, we have to find the balance, and we have adopted a calibrated approach in our system planning certain level of redundancy at national grid level, together with a higher level of redundancy for critical systems at the local level.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Critical services and infrastructure, such as lifts and traffic signalling systems, have contingency plans for power outages that might happen on the national grid.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: For example, passenger lifts must be installed with an Automatic Rescue Device, so that if there is a power failure, the lift will be parked at the nearest floor and open its doors.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: For lifts in very high-rise residential buildings or those serving both residential and non-residential uses, a standby generator is required to provide emergency power to resume at least one lift's operations.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: And our public hospitals also carry out preventive maintenance, regular maintenance, to ensure that both their electrical installations and power system backups are in good working condition.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: The Member also spoke on the importance of having a well-equipped public to respond to emergencies, and this is well-noted.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: EMA is working with the industry to review processes for handling events, such as the recent power outage, to ensure they remain satisfactory.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: During the blackout, SP Group officers were immediately activated and deployed at key substations and control centres.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: SP Group also provided the public with progressive updates on its social media channels and concurrently informed the media of updates as well.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: But as with every incident, we will review carefully to see how we can further improve our responses.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: In summary, this Bill will ensure that the Gas Act continues to remain effective and relevant in enhancing gas supply security and strengthening safeguards for such critical infrastructure.
